hints: Start by splitting the ester at the COO link, remember hydrolysis always gives a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol.
Identify your two hydrolysis products here as butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
Now think about what hot, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ does to each part, a primary alcohol is fully oxidised but a carboxylic acid resists further oxidation.
walkthrough:
**Hydrolyse the ester first**

Think of an ester as an acid joined to an alcohol. Adding water splits it back apart.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**List the intermediate mixture**

You now have two carbon compounds to oxidise. The acid part is butanoic acid and the alcohol part is ethanol, a primary alcohol.

Intermediate mixture: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$

**Apply hot, acidified KMnO4**

This is a very strong oxidising agent. Carboxylic acids are already fully oxidised, so butanoic acid is unchanged. A primary alcohol is oxidised in two stages all the way to a carboxylic acid under hot conditions.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$

**Collect the final carbon products**

Ethanol becomes ethanoic acid, while butanoic acid remains. So the final mixture contains those two acids and no alcohol remains.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is propanoic acid, which is not formed here. This comes from miscounting carbons when splitting the ester or oxidising the alcohol.
options.B: Incorrect. While $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ from ethanol is correct, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is wrong. The acid from the ester has four carbons ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$), not three.
options.C: Correct. Hydrolysis gives butanoic acid plus ethanol. Hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ leaves the acid unchanged but oxidises ethanol fully to ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. Final products are therefore ethanoic acid and butanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This is just the hydrolysis mixture with no oxidation. It forgets that hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ will oxidise the primary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.
